content: The root compound reduces the effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, and it is considered theoretical. Close monitoring is recommended. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in their metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Prednisone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which accelerates their metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which accelerates their metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of protamine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative therapies should be used due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Conjugated synthetic estrogens may decrease the effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and associated adverse effects. The mechanism of this interaction is unspecified, and its clinical significance is minor or unknown. Conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease pyridoxine (vitamin B6) levels by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreases their levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Conjugated synthetic estrogens increase ropinirole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease rose hips levels by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Roxithromycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of somapacitan by decreasing serum IGF-1 response. Patients may require higher somapacitan dosages. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. Stiripentol affects the metabolism of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting and inducing CYP1A2. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. CYP1A2 substrates may require dosage adjustments. Streptomycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Sulfisoxazole decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness if coadministered. Teicoplanin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Temocillin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Teriflunomide decreases the levels of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tigecycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tobramycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Trazodone decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Conjugated synthetic estrogens may also affect tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) effects, increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Trimethoprim decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Trimipramine may interact with conjugated synthetic estrogens through an unspecified mechanism, potentially decreasing TCA effects while increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A4 substrates according to product labeling. Conjugated synthetic estrogens decrease the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustment is recommended when coadministered with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. Vancomycin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Common adverse effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens include abdominal pain, back pain, bloating, breast enlargement, breast tenderness, headache, nausea, peripheral edema, vomiting, amenorrhea, breakthrough bleeding, corneal curvature changes, depression, diarrhea, melasma, spotting, weight changes, abdominal discomfort, abdominal distension, muscle spasms, dizziness, insomnia, breast pain, alopecia, rash, urticaria, deep vein thrombosis, and thrombosis. Contraindications include documented hypersensitivity, active or history of breast cancer, arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g., stroke, myocardial infarction), thrombophlebitis, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, thrombogenic valvular disease, protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency, or other known thrombophilic disorders.
